summary: Yellow Point, OR: 1930s cabin per firelookout.com; 1943 Army aircraft-warning observation post; 1944 tree platform; listed gone. County and dates conflict across sources.

facts.design: Cabin (1930s, per firelookout.com); tree platform (1944, per Forest Lookouts)
facts.status_note: FFLA index lists it as gone and the Forest Lookouts page marks it removed; firelookout.com says the cabin was abandoned in 1953; no source describes the site today

events.note: Cabin dated only to the 1930s; exact year not given

Fourth Fighter Command approved the site as an observation post for the Aircraft Warning Service (letter, May 4, 1943); the Army authorized activation as of noon, May 20, 1943, code name Eugene 69, to change to Charlie Zero Seven after June 1 (memorandum, May 13, 1943)
Army deactivated the observation post effective 1800 hours, October 16, 1943
Western Lane FPA constructed a tree platform at the point for a total cost of $14.65

evidence.supports: page header activation date May 29, 1943; deactivated October 16, 1943

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts page marks the site Removed

evidence.quote: Yellow Butte Yellow Point GRANT COUNTY

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts header gives May 29, 1943 as the activation date, while a May 13, 1943 memorandum on the same page gives noon, May 20. Not resolved; the story gives both.

Firelookout.com and the FFLA index both list Josephine County. The Forest Lookouts page names no county, only the Western Lane FPA and township 20S-7W-16, but its county index files Yellow Point under Douglas County. Not resolved; the story gives the county as the two listings do and notes the Douglas County index entry.
The FFLA index gives 43.82440, -123.54435. The record also holds 43.83179, -123.54288 from a second list we did not read. Not resolved; the story gives no coordinates.

notes_for_editor: Two sources describe different uses: firelookout.com a 1930s cabin abandoned 1953, the Forest Lookouts page a 1943 Army aircraft-warning observation post and a 1944 tree platform. They may describe one site at different times, but no source links them. Check the county: firelookout.com and the FFLA index say Josephine, the Forest Lookouts county index says Douglas, and the Western Lane FPA credit and township reference may point to Lane County; no source says so. The FFLA coordinates (about 43.8 N) also look well north of Josephine County, which lies near 42 N; check on a county map before the county is published. Check the coordinates against the second list in the record. The 1943 memo says the post was to get new living quarters and a woodshed; the sources do not say whether any cabin stood then.
